dimensions.name: Reference mining & contract inference

evidence.note: Listed /opt/reference/node_modules once and read pages-basic next-shims.d.ts, grounding next/server contracts (NextRequest/NextResponse/after) in the shim — genuine contract inference from fixtures.

The only touches of the reference tree are a node_modules dir listing and an ls of server-only/client-only. The vendored next-source and vite-source checkouts are never opened anywhere in the trajectory.
Layout-order semantics ('Next requires root layout outside nested layouts') asserted from memory and patched reactively, not verified against vendored Next.js source.

RSC handling, dynamicParams, cookie propagation, params-as-Promise, and root-route mapping were all inferred from memory and corrected by reading fixture pages and Playwright failure output rather than consulting upstream source.
Vite plugin/hydration behavior worked out by trial (duplicate React discovery, peer deps) rather than by studying the vendored Vite plugin API surface.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the fixture next-shims.d.ts and grounded some shim signatures in it, and continually inspected fixture spec/page files for expected behavior — more than pure memory (level 0). But it never opened the vendored Vite or Next.js source that is the heart of this dimension, and resolved every ambiguous framework semantic (layouts, RSC, caching, cookies, params) from memory plus reactive test-failure patching rather than re-consulting source. This is the 'skims a fixture shim then proceeds mostly on assumption; contracts inferred loosely' anchor at level 3, not the level-5 systematic reading of the Vite plugin API and per-subsystem shim grounding.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing

evidence.note: Early plans name most subsystems (CLI dev/build/start, SSR server, next/* shims, route scanning, middleware, SSG) and construction proceeds in a rough dependency order: package.json -> runtime -> shims -> index/plugin -> server -> CLI. Shows subsystem identification and coarse ordering, but as a bundled build, not sequenced milestones.

All subsystems are written monolithically before any verification; the first check (step 15) is the full 335-test suite rather than a thin vertical slice (one route under dev) gated before layering. No incremental subsystem done-criteria.

Post-build work is reactive, failure-driven patching loosely prioritized by 'highest remaining broad gap' (config -> metadata -> cookies -> hydration). Demonstrates impact-based ordering and subsystem awareness, but no maintained milestone plan or explicit done-criteria.
Late routing bug (root app/page mapped to /page) and repeated submit-complete/resume cycles show continued whack-a-mole with no re-planned milestone boundaries or through-line decomposition.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly identifies the major subsystems and constructs them in a coarse dependency order (shims/resolution -> server -> CLI -> build -> tests), and during fixing it prioritizes by broad impact — matching aspects of anchor 5. But it never establishes a thin, verified end-to-end slice before piling features on, front-loads a monolithic build gated only by the full suite, and maintains no explicit milestones, done-criteria, or revisited decomposition, keeping it below anchor 5 and well short of anchor 8. This places it at a 4, between the generic-list anchor (3) and the sensible-ordering-with-done-notions anchor (5).

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design

evidence.note: Ran the full suite ~5 times as a regression gate, tracking pass counts (69→113→131→149→153) rather than as a pure debugger — more than the level-3 'occasional oracle'.

Stood up fixture servers manually (vinext dev / cli.js dev) and used targeted curl probes on specific routes (API methods, cookies, sitemap, redirect, cache-control) to verify subsystem behavior between slow full runs — a designed fast-feedback loop.
Parsed playwright-env-results.json for exact failure messages; at 98 distinguished assertion mismatches from broken routes — interpreting failures by root cause, not just symptom.
Isolated the Set-Cookie bug ('works in isolation' but a dual Vite-runtime context loses it) — genuine root-cause probing characteristic of higher anchors.

Verified build path via npm run build + node --check + import + npm pack, but only the dev server path was exercised against fixtures; the production vinext build/start path was never smoke-tested, and no minimal reproductions were built for RSC/caching/actions.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent designed a real verification loop — fast targeted curl probes against manually-launched fixtures per subsystem, the full suite as a count-tracked regression gate, failure-log parsing, and root-cause interpretation (cookie isolation, assertion-vs-symptom) — which clears the level-5 anchor and reaches into the level-8 description. It falls short of a solid 8/10 because it verified only the dev path (never the production build/start of a fixture), never ran targeted Playwright subsets, and built no minimal reproductions for the hardest subsystems (RSC, use cache, server actions). That places it at a strong 7.

dimensions.name: Progress & pass-rate tracking across subsystems

evidence.note: Consistently records full-suite pass counts across runs (69→113→131→149→153) and re-runs the whole suite after each batch of changes to measure movement and catch regressions.

Parses Playwright JSON results into failure files and buckets remaining failures by subsystem (API methods, metadata, cookies, hydration, config), using that to target broad categories rather than working purely reactively.

Detects a discrepancy between passing manual smoke checks and failing suite tests, diagnoses it as stale packed fixture vs. current dist, and verifies the built dist actually contains the patches — a genuine self-check against circular debugging.

Long loop on Set-Cookie propagation with repeated retries across many steps before eventually stepping back to the duplicate-runtime/AsyncLocalStorage root cause — monitoring present but slow to break the loop.

After the last measured run (~153/325), multiple further patches (root-page mapping, nav/form delegation, counter fallback) are applied and never reconciled against the full suite; a very long repeated-submit tail proceeds with a stale whole-surface picture.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it tracks per-run pass counts, categorizes failures by subsystem, re-runs the suite to catch regressions, and even detects and diagnoses a measurement discrepancy (stale package vs. current build). But it falls short of 8-10 because its per-area view is loose rather than a maintained pass-rate-by-area model, it looped on the cookie failure for many steps before stepping back, and in the final stretch it applied numerous patches without reconciling them against the full-suite evidence, letting the done-vs-remaining picture go stale. That places it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Design revision under divergence

evidence.note: Diagnosed that declaring react/react-dom as vinext dependencies caused a duplicate React copy and invalid hook calls; reworked packaging to peerDependencies and re-ran the full suite — a genuine foundational resolution/packaging pivot with re-verification.
Reworked renderApp to await async server components before renderToString and pass plain params, revisiting a render-pipeline design decision rather than patching individual routes.

On duplicate-runtime/AsyncLocalStorage divergence: tried configFile:false (subsystem rework) but then settled for a globalThis context fallback — a workaround around the underlying multiple-instance resolution flaw rather than fixing resolution.

The custom-server render pipeline never gained real hydration despite being repeatedly identified as the top blocker; the agent piled hacks (event delegation, DOM-text refresh keyed on testids, a global counter fallback script) instead of refactoring the foundation — patching around a flawed core and drifting toward overfit.
Fixed layout-wrapping order and root page->'/' scanner bug as targeted subsystem corrections, showing local design revision but not foundational pivots.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent demonstrates clear 5-level behavior: it recognized several wrong approaches and reworked those subsystems (React peerDependencies to kill duplicate React, awaiting async components, config-file loading, layout order) rather than only patching symptoms. However it falls short of 8/10 because the single most consequential foundational choice — the SSR render pipeline lacking real client hydration — was repeatedly identified as blocking many subsystems yet never refactored; instead the agent accreted increasingly hacky workarounds (culminating in a hand-written counter fallback script) and a globalThis context shim rather than fixing module resolution. The trajectory is thus a mix of genuine subsystem reworks and a sustained failure to pivot on the core, placing it squarely at 5.

dimensions.name: Resisting overfit to the visible suite

evidence.note: Config redirects/rewrites/headers implemented as a general rule compiler (source→destination pattern matching, slug substitution, conditions) rather than hard-coding the specific fixture URLs — faithful semantics.

Fixed real Next.js contract details: params/searchParams handling, awaiting async server components, correct root-outside-nested layout wrapping order, parallel @slot/page vs @slot/default — implementing the actual framework contract, not test hacks.

Diagnosed and fixed genuinely general problems: moved react/react-dom to peerDependencies to avoid duplicate-React invalid-hook errors, shared request context via AsyncLocalStorage/globalThis for Set-Cookie — general framework-level solutions.

Reaches for fixture-specific shortcut on hard hydration behavior: injected a browser script that 'refresh[es] known DOM text for usePathname/useSearchParams if elements include obvious test IDs' — keyed to fixture markers, not real reactivity.

Blatant overfit: injects a 'lightweight global counter fallback script' handling clicks on Increment/Decrement buttons and updating '[data-testid=count]' text, explicitly because 'fixtures render predictable data-testid' — special-casing the visible counter fixture instead of real React hydration, with no note of hidden-suite risk.
No point in the trajectory reasons about the 373 hidden tests or the visible-vs-hidden gap; generalization risk is never articulated.

dimensions.reasoning: The bulk of the implementation targets real Next.js semantics — config rule matching, layout nesting order, async component awaiting, peer-dependency React sharing, AsyncLocalStorage context — which matches anchor 5's 'actual semantics rather than test-specific hacks.' But on hard behaviors (client hydration/navigation), the agent repeatedly reaches for fixture-specific shortcuts: DOM-text refresh keyed to test IDs and a counter fallback keyed to data-testid='count' and Increment/Decrement labels, explicitly justified by the fixtures' predictable markers, and never flagging the risk. It also never once reasons about the visible-vs-hidden gap. That combination — mostly general but fixture-specific shortcuts when a behavior is hard, without noting the risk — sits squarely at anchor 3, nudged to 4 by the substantial faithful-contract work elsewhere.

rubric.task_read: This is a maximally long-horizon, high-complexity build: reimplement the core of Next.js (CLI, Pages + App routers, SSR, SSG, `use cache`, server actions, middleware, `after()`, client hooks, and a Vite plugin that shims `next/*`) as a single `vinext` package on Vite's plugin API, with no internet and only vendored source to learn from. Difficulty comes from the sheer surface area, tightly-coupled subsystems, contracts that must be reverse-engineered from vendored Next.js/Vite source and fixture `next-shims.d.ts`, and a moving target (335 visible → 373 hidden tests). A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in every meta-work faculty; ceremony risk is low, thrash-and-lose-the-plot risk is very high.

dimensions.name: Reference mining & contract inference
dimensions.description: Studying vendored Vite/Next.js source and fixture type shims to understand the Vite plugin API and the exact `next/*` contracts before and while implementing, rather than guessing framework semantics.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There is no internet; correct behavior lives entirely in the vendored source and the fixtures' `next-shims.d.ts`. Guessing Next.js semantics or the Vite plugin lifecycle guarantees rework across a huge surface.

anchors.0: Starts coding shims/routing from memory of Next.js without opening any reference or fixture file.
anchors.3: Skims one or two reference files or a fixture shim, then proceeds mostly on assumption; contracts are inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Vite plugin API surface and the fixture `next-shims.d.ts` for the subsystem currently being built; grounds each `next/*` shim in an actual type signature.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the vendored Next.js source and Vite plugin hooks to the required subsystems, extracts precise contracts from every fixture shim, and re-consults source when behavior is ambiguous rather than guessing; notes non-obvious semantics (e.g. RSC boundaries, cache keys, action serialization).
anchors.10: Sustained, targeted research throughout the build: continuously cross-references upstream source to resolve edge-case semantics as they surface, distinguishes what the fixtures actually require from full Next.js behavior, and builds an accurate mental/written model of how routing, RSC, and module resolution interlock — visibly preventing whole classes of rework.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the framework into ordered, independently-verifiable subsystems (module shim/resolution, dev server, routing, SSR, SSG, caching, actions, CLI/build) with a dependency-aware sequence and done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The subsystems are tightly coupled and one package must ship all of them; without dependency-aware sequencing and explicit milestones the agent will build in an order that forces constant backtracking and never reaches a testable state.

anchors.0: Treats the whole thing as one undifferentiated coding push; no ordering or sub-goals.
anchors.3: A flat, generic list mirroring the requirement bullets, with no dependency ordering or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Identifies the major subsystems and picks a sensible order (e.g. resolution/plugin before routing before SSR/SSG), with a rough notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.8: Dependency-aware milestone plan that sequences a minimal end-to-end path (one route rendering under dev) before layering features, each milestone tied to concrete fixtures/tests that prove it, and revisited as the build reveals coupling.
anchors.10: A living decomposition that establishes a thin vertical slice early, orders remaining subsystems to maximize how soon tests can gate progress, explicitly manages interfaces between subsystems so they compose, and re-plans milestone boundaries as integration realities emerge — never losing the through-line across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design
dimensions.description: Deliberately using and extending the Playwright suite and fixture apps as checks — running targeted subsets per subsystem, building smaller probes, and verifying behavior beyond just 'it compiles'.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 335-test suite is the ground truth, but it is slow and coarse; verifying each subsystem needs faster, targeted checks and running the right fixtures, or the agent flies blind between rare full-suite runs.

anchors.0: Never runs the test suite or the fixture apps; assumes correctness from the code alone.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally as a pass/fail oracle with no targeted or intermediate verification.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets / individual fixtures for the subsystem in progress and uses failures to guide fixes; verifies dev and build paths work.
anchors.8: Designs a verification loop: fast targeted checks per subsystem, standing up fixtures manually to observe SSR/SSG/action behavior, and using the suite as a regression gate rather than a debugger; confirms both `dev` and the production `build`/`start` paths.
anchors.10: Builds a deliberate, layered verification strategy — minimal reproductions for hard subsystems (RSC, caching, actions), interprets test failures by root cause rather than symptom, and actively probes behaviors the visible suite may under-cover, treating passing tests as necessary-not-sufficient evidence of a faithful reimplementation.

dimensions.name: Progress & pass-rate tracking across subsystems
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, current picture of which subsystems/tests pass vs. remain, and detecting circular debugging or regressions across a very large surface.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of tests and many interdependent subsystems over a long horizon, it is easy to fix one area while regressing another, or to loop on the same failure; an accurate done-vs-remaining picture is what sustains forward motion.

anchors.0: No tracking of what passes or what is left; works reactively with no sense of overall state.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; notices only whatever failure is in front of it.
anchors.5: Tracks pass counts / which subsystems are done and which are pending, and re-checks after changes to catch obvious regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains a structured, updated view of pass-rate by area, watches for regressions when touching shared code, and recognizes when it is looping on one failure and steps back rather than retrying blindly.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles a precise model of done-vs-remaining against real test evidence across the whole surface, catches subtle cross-subsystem regressions early, quantifies progress toward the full suite, and reallocates effort to the highest-leverage remaining failures rather than drifting.

dimensions.name: Design revision under divergence
dimensions.description: Revising the architecture or approach (module resolution scheme, rendering pipeline, cache/action wiring) when reality — failing tests or discovered semantics — contradicts the initial design, rather than patching around a flawed foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early architectural choices (how `next/*` is intercepted, how RSC/SSR is wired into Vite) will be partly wrong; the agent must be willing to refactor the foundation instead of piling hacks that make later subsystems impossible.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on the original approach even as failures accumulate; only adds patches.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when something breaks but never revisits an underlying design decision even when it is clearly the cause.
anchors.5: Recognizes when an approach is wrong and reworks that subsystem, absorbing the cost rather than hacking around it.
anchors.8: Detects when a foundational choice (resolution, render pipeline) is blocking multiple subsystems and refactors it deliberately, updating the plan and re-verifying dependents afterward.
anchors.10: Treats falsified assumptions as signals to rethink the design cleanly, weighs refactor-vs-workaround explicitly, executes foundational pivots without losing already-passing behavior, and emerges with a more coherent architecture — demonstrating sustained self-correction across the horizon.

dimensions.name: Resisting overfit to the visible suite
dimensions.description: Implementing faithful, general framework behavior rather than special-casing the 335 visible tests, given explicit notice that 373 hidden tests over the same behavior will judge the work.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec openly states the final grade uses a larger hidden suite covering the same behaviors; an agent that hard-codes to visible fixtures will pass locally and fail the real metric, so recognizing and countering this gap is a distinct, decisive meta-work demand.

anchors.0: Hard-codes outputs or narrowly special-cases the visible fixtures/tests to turn them green.
anchors.3: Mostly general but reaches for a fixture-specific shortcut when a behavior is hard, without noting the risk.
anchors.5: Implements the actual semantics for each behavior rather than test-specific hacks, aware the suite is a sample not the target.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about the visible-vs-hidden gap, generalizes each subsystem to the real Next.js contract from the reference, and avoids overfitting even under schedule pressure.
anchors.10: Systematically implements to the general contract inferred from upstream source and shim types, stress-tests behaviors beyond what the visible tests exercise to expose overfit, and can articulate why the implementation should hold on unseen cases of the same behavior.
